quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Coordinating Conjunctions — Result
quests.contextSentence: The bridge was closed for repairs, ___ traffic backed up for miles.
quests.completedSentence: The bridge was closed for repairs, so traffic backed up for miles.
quests.ruleExplanation: A common slip is reaching for 'because' here, but that would wrongly suggest the traffic caused the closure. The closure came first and caused the traffic, so 'so' is needed to show that direction.
quests.nativeTip: The closure is the cause; what's needed here is the word for what actually followed from it.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Coordinating Conjunctions — Result
quests.contextSentence: Ticket sales dropped sharply, ___ the theater cut back to three shows a week.
quests.completedSentence: Ticket sales dropped sharply, so the theater cut back to three shows a week.
quests.ruleExplanation: Choosing 'because' here would reverse the logic, implying the schedule cut caused the sales drop. Since the sales drop came first, 'so' is what correctly introduces the resulting cutback.
quests.nativeTip: The drop in sales is the cause; the schedule cut is what followed from it.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Coordinating Conjunctions — Result
quests.contextSentence: The negotiations collapsed at the last minute, ___ both sides walked away with nothing.
quests.completedSentence: The negotiations collapsed at the last minute, so both sides walked away with nothing.
quests.ruleExplanation: Picking 'because' here would mistakenly suggest walking away caused the collapse. Since the collapse happened first, 'so' correctly introduces the outcome that followed.
quests.nativeTip: The collapse is the cause; walking away empty-handed is what actually happened as a result.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Subordinating Conjunctions — Reason
quests.contextSentence: The store closed early ___ a burst pipe flooded the back room.

quests.nativeTip: The flood is the explanation for the early closing, not the other way around.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Subordinating Conjunctions — Reason
quests.contextSentence: The flight was rerouted ___ severe turbulence was reported ahead.
quests.completedSentence: The flight was rerouted because severe turbulence was reported ahead.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Subordinating Conjunctions — Condition
quests.contextSentence: ___ you don't submit the form by Friday, your application won't be processed.
quests.completedSentence: If you don't submit the form by Friday, your application won't be processed.
quests.ruleExplanation: Since this clause already contains 'don't', adding 'unless' on top would create a confusing double negative. 'If' is the clean, correct way to state this negative condition.
quests.nativeTip: The clause already has 'don't' in it — check whether adding another negative word would confuse the meaning.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Subordinating Conjunctions — Condition
quests.contextSentence: ___ she doesn't confirm by noon, we'll release her seat to the waitlist.
quests.completedSentence: If she doesn't confirm by noon, we'll release her seat to the waitlist.
quests.ruleExplanation: With 'doesn't' already in the clause, 'unless' would double up the negative meaning awkwardly. 'If' keeps the sentence clear and correct.
quests.nativeTip: The clause already contains 'doesn't' — adding 'unless' here would stack two negatives together.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Subordinating Conjunctions — Condition
quests.contextSentence: The gym stays open, ___ there's a public holiday, in which case hours are shorter.
quests.completedSentence: The gym stays open, unless there's a public holiday, in which case hours are shorter.
quests.ruleExplanation: Here the following clause is positive, not negative, which is exactly the pattern 'unless' is built for: it already carries its own built-in negative meaning.
quests.nativeTip: This time the clause after the blank is positive, which is the pattern a word with its own built-in negative meaning needs.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Subordinating Conjunctions — Reason
quests.contextSentence: The bakery stayed open late ___ demand was unusually high that evening.
quests.completedSentence: The bakery stayed open late because demand was unusually high that evening.
quests.ruleExplanation: It's tempting to reach for 'although' out of habit, but nothing here contradicts anything else — high demand is simply the plain reason for staying open, which 'because' correctly introduces.
quests.nativeTip: Check carefully: is anything here actually surprising or contradictory, or is this just a plain explanation?

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Subordinating Conjunctions — Concession
quests.contextSentence: ___ the team lost their star player to injury, they still made the playoffs.
quests.completedSentence: Although the team lost their star player to injury, they still made the playoffs.
quests.ruleExplanation: Unlike the previous case, this one genuinely involves a contradiction: losing a star player should have hurt their chances, yet they still succeeded, which is exactly what 'although' is for.
quests.nativeTip: This time, losing a key player really should have hurt their chances — but it didn't.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Subordinating Conjunctions — Reason
quests.contextSentence: The flight was delayed ___ a mechanical issue was found during inspection.
quests.completedSentence: The flight was delayed because a mechanical issue was found during inspection.

quests.nativeTip: Check again: is there a real contradiction here, or is this simply stating the plain cause?

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Subordinating Conjunctions — Time
quests.contextSentence: The smoke alarm went off ___ someone burned toast in the kitchen.
quests.completedSentence: The smoke alarm went off when someone burned toast in the kitchen.
quests.ruleExplanation: It's easy to default to 'while' for anything time-related, but this is a single triggering instant, not an overlapping stretch, so 'when' is the accurate choice.
quests.nativeTip: This is one sharp instant reaction, not two things stretching out together over time.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Subordinating Conjunctions — Time

quests.completedSentence: She reviewed her notes while she waited for the interview to start.

quests.nativeTip: This time, both activities really do stretch out together over the same period.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Subordinating Conjunctions — Time

quests.completedSentence: The screen froze when the update reached ninety percent.

quests.nativeTip: This happened at one specific triggering point, not across a stretch of overlapping time.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Correlative Conjunctions — Alternatives
quests.contextSentence: You can either take the highway ___ the scenic route — both get you there around the same time.
quests.completedSentence: You can either take the highway or the scenic route — both get you there around the same time.
quests.ruleExplanation: A common mix-up is pairing 'either' with 'nor', but 'either' only ever pairs with 'or'; 'nor' belongs exclusively with 'neither'.
quests.nativeTip: 'Either' has only one correct partner, no matter how tempting 'nor' might feel.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Correlative Conjunctions — Alternatives
quests.contextSentence: The workshop is either fully virtual ___ hybrid this year, depending on demand.
quests.completedSentence: The workshop is either fully virtual or hybrid this year, depending on demand.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Either' locks in 'or' regardless of what the two options are, so the pairing never changes to 'nor' here.
quests.nativeTip: No matter what the two options are, 'either' always needs the same one partner word.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Correlative Conjunctions — Alternatives
quests.contextSentence: Either the shipment left the warehouse already ___ it's still sitting in customs — we're trying to find out which.
quests.completedSentence: Either the shipment left the warehouse already or it's still sitting in customs — we're trying to find out which.
quests.ruleExplanation: Even with two full clauses as the options, 'either' still requires 'or', never 'nor', to complete the pair correctly.
quests.nativeTip: Whatever the two possibilities are, 'either' still only ever completes with the same one word.

quests.nativeTip: 'Neither' has only one correct partner, even though 'or' might feel like the natural fit.

quests.nativeTip: That winning streak should have been more than enough — check whether the outcome matched that expectation.
